info.name: England Orders — Staff App API
info.description:
API behind the England Orders staff app (internal team, admin accounts). Source of truth: fmcg_orders, fmcg_customers, fmcg_order_items; the app writes only fmcg_order_deliveries (delivery date, Pandi, Adda, Builty images). No prices are returned. Order status, quantities, prices and stock are never changed.

Every response uses one envelope (same as the Masoom app API): `{error, message, code, data}`; `code` equals the HTTP status; failures carry a stable `data.reason` (and `data.fields` for validation). Examples are real responses captured from the local test server (tokens/signatures redacted).

**Accountrix ERP sales (v1.3).** Posted ERP sales are listed with website orders. The England backend pulls them from the ERP's read-only feed (`GET {ERP}/api/integrations/england/sales`, server-to-server bearer token, never sent to the app) into `fmcg_erp_sales` — one row per ERP sale (unique `erp_sale_id`), keeping the ERP invoice number, customer, date and net total. ERP sales are NOT copied into fmcg_orders and the ERP is never written. Every list card and detail carries `origin` (`website` | `erp`) and a unique `key` (`web-<id>` / `erp-<id>`); ids are only unique within one origin, so ERP records are opened via `/app/erp-sales/{id}`. Delivery date, Pandi, Adda and Builty images for an ERP sale are stored in England's `fmcg_erp_sale_deliveries`.

Examples come from the local integration rig (TEST records created through the real website order service and the real ERP SaleService). Ids in your database will differ: take them from `GET /app/orders`.
